articles.title: Fed officials divided on US inflation views; US home prices hit all-time high
articles.content: The International Monetary Fund predicts a modest global economic growth of three percent for this year. In the United States, home prices have soared to unprecedented levels, creating challenges for prospective buyers. The Federal Reserve is experiencing internal disagreements about future interest rate policies and inflation management. Moreover, a decline in global oil demand is anticipated for the first time since 2020.

articles.title: Dmart recasts strategy as rapid delivery competition intensifies
articles.content: DMart has scaled back its e-commerce footprint, exiting underperforming cities to focus on metros as competition intensifies in India’s rapid delivery space. Despite rising pressure from Amazon, Flipkart, Zepto and Swiggy, the retailer is sticking to its low-cost model and non-10-minute delivery approach amid muted earnings performance.

articles.title: Korea’s world-beating stocks are now trading cheaper than ever
articles.content: South Korea's benchmark Kospi index has surged about 80% this year to record highs, yet its valuation has fallen to a historic low as corporate earnings, led by memory-chip giants Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, have outpaced the rally. Investors remain divided over whether the cheap valuations present a buying opportunity or reflect concerns over the sustainability of the AI-driven memory boom.

articles.title: Nearly 60% of foreign inflows into India-focused funds withdrawn since 2024 peak: Report
articles.content: Foreign investors have withdrawn nearly sixty percent of funds from India-focused equity. This capital shift is driven by global artificial intelligence investment opportunities and momentum. Investors pulled nine billion dollars from India funds in calendar year twenty twenty six. Gold funds saw a modest inflow after significant outflows, while US equities attracted fresh investment. Europe also registered its first weekly inflow in nearly three months.

articles.title: George Goodman’s investing wisdom: Why sometimes the best move is to do nothing
articles.content: George Goodman's classic book highlights investor psychology over pure logic.  He stressed knowing oneself and avoiding crowd mentality for better decisions.  Patience and thoughtful inaction often prove more profitable than impulsive trading.  Greed and fear drive market cycles, leading many to buy high and sell low.  Goodman's insights remain relevant for navigating today's volatile financial markets.

articles.title: Could oil prices spike further? Inside the fragile US-Iran stance in the Gulf
articles.content: Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East have escalated after attacks on commercial vessels.  Iran's objective appears to be expanding its strategic influence over the Strait of Hormuz.  Gulf nations are remaining cautious to avoid direct involvement in the confrontation.  Crude oil prices are expected to remain elevated due to ongoing geopolitical risks.  India, a major oil importer, faces increased vulnerability from these market developments.
